originalTitle: Violent crypto attacks rise as criminals hunt bigger payouts
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news: There's been a big increase in physical attacks on people who own cryptocurrency, with a 33% rise in the first half of 2026. This means that criminals are using violence to steal digital money from people, and the total amount stolen has reached $124 million. These attacks are happening all over the world, but France is seeing the most problems. This matters because it shows that owning cryptocurrency can be risky, not just because of market fluctuations, but also because of physical threats. Overall, it's a warning that cryptocurrency owners need to be careful and protect themselves from potential dangers.

originalTitle: IDFC First Bank Q1 Results: Profit shoots up 132% YoY to record Rs 1,075 crore; NII jumps 21%
simplifiedContent: IDFC First Bank just announced its financial results for the first quarter of the year, and they're very good. The bank made a profit of Rs 1,075 crore, which is 132% more than it made during the same time last year. This is the highest quarterly profit the bank has ever reported. The bank's net interest income (NII) also increased by 21%, which is a key measure of how well the bank is doing. This matters because it shows that the bank is performing well and making more money than it was before.

originalTitle: Govt of Singapore’s India portfolio: 7 stocks rally up to 135% in CY26
simplifiedContent: The Government of Singapore has investments in 39 Indian companies, and the total value of these investments decreased by 25% to Rs 1,51,353 crore in June 2026. Despite this decline, some of these investments did very well, with one company called Aditya Infotech increasing in value by 137%. On the other hand, some bigger investments like HDFC Bank and Syngene International didn't do as well, which brought down the overall performance of the portfolio. This news matters because it shows how the Government of Singapore's investments in India are performing, and which companies are doing well or poorly. The big gains in some stocks, like Aditya Infotech, are noteworthy, even if the overall portfolio value decreased.

originalTitle: Metals Fluctuate as Middle East Escalation Keeps Bulls in Check
simplifiedContent: The prices of metals like copper and aluminum went up and down recently. This happened because there's a possibility of more conflict in the Middle East, which could affect the global economy. As a result, investors who think prices will go up (called "bulls") are being cautious and not buying as much as they might have otherwise. This means that the prices of metals aren't rising as quickly as they might have. The uncertainty about what will happen in the Middle East is keeping metal prices from going up too much.

originalTitle: Big Tech Debt Flood Is Taking Over Risk In Market: Credit Weekly
simplifiedContent: Some of the biggest technology companies are borrowing a lot of money by selling bonds to invest in artificial intelligence (AI). This is creating a large wave of new debt in the market. As a result, these tech companies are having a significant impact on the US corporate bond market. This matters because it shows how much influence Big Tech has on the market and how their borrowing habits can affect the overall economy. The large amount of debt from these companies is changing the risk landscape of the market.

originalTitle: IDFC First Bank Q1 Results 2026: Net profit surges 132% to  ₹1,075 crore; NII rises 21%
simplifiedContent: IDFC First Bank just released its quarterly results, showing a big increase in profit. The bank's net profit jumped 132% to ₹1,075 crore, which means it made a lot more money than it did during the same time last year. This happened because the bank earned more from interest on loans and had to set aside less money for potential losses. The bank's customer business also grew, with more people taking out loans and depositing money, which is a positive sign for the bank's future. This is good news for investors, as it suggests the bank is doing well and may continue to grow.
